posts.central_knowledge_unit: Roberto Carlos' Brazil free kick in 1997: The physics behind 'impossible' strike - ESPN
posts.claim: Roberto Carlos’s 3 June 1997 free kick for Brazil against France can be explained by ordinary aerodynamics rather than having “defied physics”: side-spin creates aerodynamic lift, while drag reduces the ball’s forward speed; over a sufficiently long, powerful shot, the changing balance can make the path bend much more sharply late in flight. The 2010 physics paper treats Carlos’s roughly 35-m kick as an interpretation/application of its spinning-ball-spiral model, not as a direct reconstruction of that individual kick.
posts.headline: Physics Explains Roberto Carlos' 1997 Free‑Kick Curve
